sources.title: Mikhail Khovanov, Triply-graded link homology and Hochschild homology of Soergel bimodules, arXiv:math/0510265v3 (28 May 2006), 19 printed pages; published as Internat. J. Math. 18 (2007) 869-885
sources.locator: Complete 19-page article: 'Hochschild homology' printed pp. 1-3; 'Soergel bimodules' pp. 3-4; 'Soergel bimodules and a braid group action (after Raphael Rouquier)' pp. 4-5; 'Graphical presentation' p. 6; 'Link homology' pp. 6-7; 'Sketch of proof' pp. 7-10 (Theorem 1, Lemma 1, the a=0 reduction, the (1,-1,0) correction and trigrading paragraph); 'Hecke algebras, Soergel bimodules and Kazhdan-Lusztig theory' pp. 10-14; 'Bimodules B_w and link homology' pp. 14-15; 'Example: m=2 and sigma=sigma_1^n' pp. 15-16; final remarks pp. 16-17.

read_evidence.method: Full 19-page PDF (190287 bytes, sha256_16 548a0eece08bd967) downloaded from arXiv and text-extracted with MuPDF; every section was read in the extracted text, and the proof of Theorem 1 (pp. 7-9), the trigrading paragraph (p. 10) and the m=2 example (pp. 15-16) were read line by line against the extracted text.

contents.name: Definition of Hochschild homology via R-coinvariants and the derived functors Tor^{R^e}_i(R,M), and the resolution recipe (printed pp. 1-2)
The standard bar resolution of a k-algebra by free R-bimodules (printed p. 2)
The Koszul resolution of a polynomial algebra R=k[y_1,...,y_m] over R^e and the explicit complex computing HH(R,M) (printed p. 2)
The duality HH_i(R,M) = HH^{m-i}(R,M) for polynomial rings and the remark that Hochschild cohomology may replace Hochschild homology (printed pp. 2-3)
contents.reason: The Tor/Ext duality of the polynomial ring is part of the published Hochschild development; this pair uses the Tor degree throughout and only quotes the duality for the sign in the trigrading dictionary.

contents.name: Figure 1 diagrammatic calculus: bimodules as boxes, tensor products by concatenation, closure of ends as Hochschild homology (printed p. 3)

Soergel bimodules: the rings R'=Q[x_1,...,x_m] and R'_i=Q[x_1,...,x_i+x_{i+1},x_ix_{i+1},...], the bimodules B'_i=R'\otimes_{R'_i}R', their rank-two freeness, and the definition of Soergel bimodules (printed pp. 3-4)
The degree-preserving bimodule homomorphisms br'_i:B'_i\to R' and rb'_i:R'{2}\to B'_i with rb'_i(1)=(x_i-x_{i+1})\otimes1+1\otimes(x_i-x_{i+1}) (printed p. 4)

The reduced ring R=Q[x_1-x_2,...,x_{m-1}-x_m], the invariant rings R_i, the bimodules B_i=R\otimes_{R_i}R, and the tensor-product identifications R'=R\otimes Q[x_1], R'_i\cong R_i\otimes Q[x_1], B'_i\cong B_i\otimes Q[x_1] (printed p. 4)
The example m=2: R=Q[y], R_1=Q[y^2], B_1=Q[y]\otimes_{Q[y^2]}Q[y] and rb_1(1)=y\otimes1+1\otimes y (printed p. 4)
Rouquier's braid group action: the generator complexes F(sigma_i) and F(sigma_i^{-1}) and Proposition 1 (printed pp. 4-5)
F(sigma) as the tensor product of generator complexes, the category B(R) of complexes up to homotopy, and the resulting weak braid action (printed p. 5)
Graphical presentation: R and B_i as diagrams, tensor product as composition, closure as Hochschild homology (printed p. 6)
Link homology: the complex of Hochschild homologies HH(R,F^j(sigma)) and the triply graded groups HHH(sigma) (printed pp. 6-7)
Theorem 1: up to an overall shift HHH is a link invariant and is isomorphic to the reduced homology H(sigma) of Khovanov-Rozansky II (printed p. 7)
The a=0 specialization of every arc and wide-edge factorization and the layer-by-layer Koszul sequence of the resolution (printed pp. 7-8)
The wide-edge Koszul complex of (x_1+x_2-x_3-x_4, x_1x_2-x_3x_4): its cohomology is concentrated in the top degree and equals B'_1 (printed p. 8)
Lemma 1: the first rm elements of the (r+1)m-element sequence form a regular sequence (printed p. 8)
The quotient of the polynomial ring by the first rm elements is naturally B'(D), the tensor product of the simple Soergel bimodules of the resolution (printed pp. 8-9)
The Koszul complex of the remaining m elements x_{0,j}-x_{r,j} computes the Hochschild homology of B'(D) (printed p. 9)
Downsizing from the m variables to their differences: the isomorphism between the reduced homology CH(D) and the Hochschild homology of B(D), compatible over all resolutions D (printed p. 9)

The trigrading paragraph: the built-in shift (-1,1,0), the matching of the third gradings, the Hochschild grading versus the Koszul grading with the minus sign, and the second grading as deg(x_i) minus the Hochschild grading (printed pp. 9-10)
The statement that the Euler characteristic of HHH is the HOMFLYPT link polynomial (printed p. 7)
The Iwahori-Hecke algebra presentation, the Kazhdan-Lusztig bases, Proposition 2 and the positivity Proposition 3 with its perverse-sheaf proof (printed pp. 10-11)
contents.reason: Kazhdan-Lusztig positivity and its geometric (perverse-sheaf, mixed-Hodge) proof are not used by the HHH comparison; the library's Hecke categorification page owns the Hecke algebra and importing that technology is outside this pair.

contents.name: Soergel's Proposition 4 (B_i tensor B_i, the three-term relation, far commutativity), the bimodules B_{i,i+1}, and the Kazhdan-Lusztig basis of H_3 (printed pp. 11-12)
contents.reason: These Soergel tensor-product relations are the input to the Rouquier braid relations, which the in-run Rouquier pair scaffolds and proves; this pair only uses the resulting well-definedness of the complex.

contents.name: The indecomposable bimodules B_w and the categorification of the Hecke algebra (printed pp. 12-13)
contents.reason: The indecomposable Soergel bimodules and Hecke categorification are owned by the published type-A Soergel page; this pair uses only the simple-reflection bimodules and their tensor products.

contents.name: Geometric interpretation of the B_w via equivariant intersection cohomology of Schubert varieties and the flag variety (printed pp. 13-14)
contents.reason: The equivariant-intersection-cohomology model of Soergel bimodules belongs to geometric representation theory and is not used anywhere in the HHH comparison constructed on this page.

contents.name: Bimodules B_w and link homology: decomposition of the Rouquier terms into indecomposables, the minimal complex F_min(sigma) and the reduction algorithm (printed pp. 14-15)
Example m=2, sigma=sigma_1^n: the minimal complex, the HH_0 and HH_1 complexes, their cohomology, and rank n for the (2,n) torus link (printed pp. 15-16)
Final remarks: the complexity of the m=3 endomorphism algebra and the comparison with Gornik-Rasmussen and the GSV/DGR conjectures (printed pp. 16-17)
contents.reason: These are motivation and outlook comments with no result used by the pair; the corresponding computations are explicitly described in the source as beyond its scope and would need the Fock-space recursion theory.

sources.title: Eugene Gorsky, Oscar Kivinen and Jose Simental, Algebra and geometry of link homology: Lecture notes from the IHES 2021 Summer School, Bull. London Math. Soc. 55 (2023) 537-591
sources.locator: Sections 1-3 (printed pp. 537-550, PDF pp. 1-14): section 1 introduction and organization; section 2 background on link invariants (braid group, Alexander and Markov theorems); section 3 Khovanov-Rozansky homology (3.1 Soergel bimodules and Rouquier complexes, 3.2 Khovanov-Rozansky homology, 3.3 recursions and parity, 3.4 examples). Sections 4-7 (braid varieties, y-ification, affine Springer theory, Hilbert schemes; printed pp. 551-591) were not read and lie outside the harvested range.

read_evidence.method: Full 55-page PDF (517806 bytes, sha256_16 e1b3c55a5bf27090) downloaded from the author-hosted URL and text-extracted with MuPDF; sections 1-3 (PDF pp. 1-14) were read in full, including the trigrading list of Definition 3.15, Theorem 3.16 and the computations of Examples 3.12, 3.18 and 3.23.

contents.name: Section 2: braid groups, positive and negative crossings, Alexander's theorem and Markov's theorem with the conjugation and stabilization moves (printed pp. 540-541)
contents.reason: The Alexander and Markov infrastructure is owned by the published braid-closure page and is consumed here only through the Khovanov-Rozansky invariance theorem.

contents.name: Section 3.1: R=Q[x_1,...,x_n], deg(x_i)=2, the (r)-grading shift with M(1)_d=M_{d+1}, and the bimodule B_i=R\otimes_{R^{s_i}}R(1) (printed pp. 541-542)
Lemma 3.4: B_i\otimes_R B_i is isomorphic to B_i(1)\oplus B_i(-1) (printed p. 542)
Example 3.5 and Lemma 3.4's neighbours: the three-term relation B_iB_{i+1}B_i \simeq B_i\oplus B_{i,i+1} with B_{i,i+1}=R\otimes_{R^{s_i,s_{i+1}}}R(3) (printed p. 542)
contents.reason: The rank-two decomposition is proved on the published type-A Soergel page; this pair only records that the Rouquier braid relations are available there.

contents.name: Lemma 3.8: the projection B_i(-1)\to R and the well-defined bimodule map R\to B_i(1) sending 1 to 2(x_i-x'_{i+1}), together with Remark 3.9 (printed p. 543)
Formulas (3.3)-(3.4): the Rouquier complexes T_i=[B_i(-1)\to R] and T_i^{-1}=[R\to B_i(1)], Rouquier's Theorem 3.10, Lemma 3.11 and the braid-word complex T_beta (printed pp. 544-545)
Section 3.2: the Hochschild cohomology H^i(M)=Ext^i_{R-bimod}(R,M), its termwise extension to complexes, and Remarks 3.13-3.14 on additivity and representability (printed pp. 545-546)
Definition 3.15: HHH(beta)=H(H(T_beta)) and the trigrading list (Q = internal degree with deg x_i=2, T = homological degree in the Rouquier complex, A = Hochschild degree) (printed p. 546)

Theorem 3.16: HHH is a link invariant up to an overall grading shift; it is invariant under conjugation and positive stabilization, while negative stabilization shifts it up by one A-degree (printed p. 546)
Remark 3.17: fixing the grading ambiguity to obtain an honest invariant (printed p. 546)
contents.reason: Fixing an absolute (fractional) normalization is not claimed by this pair; the pair records invariance up to an overall trigrading shift, with no silent normalization.

contents.name: Example 3.18: the termwise complexes Hom(R,T_i^k) with differentials alternating between 0 and x_i-x_{i+1} (printed pp. 546-547)
Theorem 3.19: the Elias-Hogancamp-Mellit recursion for the Khovanov-Rozansky homology of positive torus links, and Example 3.20 (q,t-Catalan polynomial) (printed p. 547)
contents.reason: The recursion theory (Fock spaces, K_n complexes, parity vanishing) is a substantial separate development not needed for the termwise-versus-hyperhomology comparison of this pair.

contents.name: The change of variables q=Q^2, t=T^2Q^{-2}, a=A Q^{-2} and the resulting Poincare-polynomial presentations (printed pp. 547-548)
Example 3.22 and Lemma 3.24: the complex K_2 and the exact-triple parity splitting used in the recursive computation (printed p. 548)
contents.reason: The K_2/K_n complex technology is part of the recursion machinery; this pair's two-strand examples are computed directly from the minimal complex and do not consume it.

contents.name: Theorem 3.25: the recursion p(v,w) computing the triply graded homology of T(m,n) (printed p. 549)
contents.reason: The torus-link recursion is a general computation theorem for a different method; no item of this pair states or uses it, and it would need its own scaffolding and sources.

contents.name: Example 3.23: the Poincare polynomials of the A=0 part of HHH(T(2,2)) and HHH(T(2,3)), and the general two-strand formula (printed pp. 547-548)
Examples 3.26-3.28: the (2,m) recursion, the (3,3) resolution and the (3,4) homology (printed pp. 549-550)
contents.reason: Higher torus links and the recursive resolution of (3,4) need the recursion theory and exceed the pair's promised examples, which stop at the two-strand family.

sources.title: Anna Beliakova, Krzysztof K. Putyra and Stephan M. Wehrli, Quantum link homology via trace functor I, arXiv:1605.03523v2 (27 Sep 2018), 85 printed pages
sources.locator: Section 3.8 (printed pp. 36-39): 3.8.2 the space of coinvariants; 3.8.3 twisted coinvariants; 3.8.4 Hochschild homology, equations (3.36)-(3.40); 3.8.5 quantum Hochschild homology, equations (3.41)-(3.43); 3.8.6 the functor HHH, equation (3.44) and Corollary 3.22.

read_evidence.method: Full 85-page PDF (1033557 bytes, sha256_16 3781e14d2bde557c) downloaded from arXiv and text-extracted with MuPDF; sections 3.8.2-3.8.6 were read in full in the extracted text, with equations (3.36)-(3.44) checked against the extraction.

contents.name: Sections 3.8.2-3.8.3: coinvariants and twisted coinvariants as symmetric shadows with the standard cyclicity twist (printed pp. 36-37)
contents.reason: The symmetric-shadow and horizontal-trace formalism is a general framework; this pair uses only the componentwise Hochschild construction and its comparison with the bar resolution.

contents.name: Section 3.8.4: the Hochschild complex CH_bullet(A,M)=coInv(M\otimes_A R_bullet(A)) with differential (3.36) and HH_0=coInv(M) (printed pp. 37-38)
Section 3.8.4: the two projective resolutions (3.37)-(3.38) and the cyclicity homotopy equivalences (3.39) (printed p. 38)
contents.reason: The cyclic-tensor comparison and its homotopy equivalences are the subject of the published Hochschild hyperhomology page, which this pair lists among its prerequisites.

contents.name: Section 3.8.4: the twisted Hochschild complex with differential (3.40) and its cyclic-tensor compatibility (printed p. 38)
contents.reason: Twisted coefficients (an automorphism phi in the differential) are not used by the pair; the trigraded comparison of this page uses untwisted Hochschild homology throughout.

contents.name: Section 3.8.5: the quantum Hochschild complex (3.41)-(3.43), its non-involutive cyclicity and quantum Hochschild homology (printed p. 39)
contents.reason: The q-deformed quantum Hochschild theory leads to quantum/annular link homology, a different invariant; the pair's comparison is with the ordinary triply graded Khovanov-Rozansky homology.

contents.name: Section 3.8.6: extension of Hochschild homology to complexes, the componentwise construction (3.44) and its description as the second page of the bicomplex spectral sequence (printed p. 39)
Section 3.8.6: the quantum Lefschetz shadow and Corollary 3.22 on the endomorphism of qHH_0(k) (printed p. 39)
contents.reason: The quantum Lefschetz trace and its q-weighting are part of the quantum/annular development and are not used in the untwisted comparison of this pair.

sources.title: Mikhail Khovanov and Lev Rozansky, Matrix factorizations and link homology II, arXiv:math/0505056v2 (31 Jan 2006), 37 printed pages; published as Geom. Topol. 12 (2008) 1387-1425
sources.locator: Section 1 (printed pp. 1-12) and section 7 (printed pp. 35-36): formulas (1)-(6), Figure 6, the crossing complexes, the complex C(D) and the homology H(D), the Markov moves (a)-(c), Theorem 1, the function F with its Markov and skein relations, formula (7), Theorem 2, the reduced-groups bullet and the remaining bullets of section 1, and the Euler-characteristic relations of section 7.

read_evidence.method: Full 37-page PDF (303442 bytes, sha256_16 1b6580406c3d35b5) downloaded from arXiv and text-extracted with MuPDF; section 1 was read in the extracted text through the braid-closure and reduced-theory bullets, and section 7 through the proof of Theorem 2.

contents.name: Section 1: matrix factorizations with a potential, the bigrading deg a=(2,0), deg x_i=(0,2), differentials of bidegree (1,1), morphisms and homotopies (formulas (1)-(2))
contents.reason: The matrix-factorization formalism is scaffolded by the in-run matrix-factorization pair; this pair consumes its crossing complexes and homology through the requires list.

contents.name: Section 1: the arc factorization and the wide-edge tensor factorization with their potentials (formulas (2)-(4))
contents.reason: The arc and wide-edge factorizations, their shifts and potentials are defined on the in-run matrix-factorization page and are used here only through the a=0 specialization.

contents.name: Section 1: the maps chi_0, chi_1 between the arc and wide-edge complexes and Figure 6 (formulas (5)-(6))
contents.reason: The explicit matrices of chi_0 and chi_1 and the corrected negative crossing are scaffolded by the matrix-factorization pair; this pair uses their induced maps on the a=0 Koszul complexes.

contents.name: Section 1: the positive and negative crossing complexes, the complex C(D) of a braid diagram, and the homology H(D) with the removal of contractible summands
contents.reason: The crossing complexes and the trigraded braid homology are the in-run matrix-factorization pair's construction, which this pair takes as its Khovanov-Rozansky side.

contents.name: Section 1: the Markov moves (a)-(c) for braid diagrams and Theorem 1 (invariance of H(D) up to an overall trigrading shift)
Section 1: the function F, its Markov relations, the skein relation, formula (7) and the HOMFLYPT identification; Theorem 2 on the Euler characteristic
End of section 1: passing from Q[a,x_1,...,x_m] to the ring Q[a,x_2-x_1,...,x_m-x_1] and the definition of the reduced cohomology groups Hbar(D) with H(D)=Hbar(D)\otimes Q[x] (printed pp. 11-12)
End of section 1: in the reduced theory the unknot has one-dimensional cohomology groups (printed p. 12)
Section 1: the remark that Reidemeister IIb is not proved and that the theory is defined on braid diagrams, and the discussion of cobordism non-extension
contents.reason: The scope restriction to braid diagrams and the failed IIb/cobordism extensions are recorded on the in-run matrix-factorization page, which owns the crossing-complex scope.

contents.name: Section 1: the deformation by lower-order terms, the sl(n) and U(n)-equivariant generalizations, and the Lee/Gornik comparison
contents.reason: Deformed and equivariant link homologies are different invariants not used by the HHH comparison; the pair works with the undeformed potential a(x_1+...+x_m) and its a=0 specialization.

contents.name: Section 7: the cone relations for Euler characteristics of C(D sigma_i^{+-1}) and the proof of Theorem 2
Section 7: the specialization q sqrt(alpha)=1 yielding the Alexander polynomial
contents.reason: The Alexander specialization corresponds to the sl(1) theory and is not used in the HHH-HOMFLYPT comparison; no item of the pair states Alexander homology.

contents.name: Section 7: the Gukov-Schwarz-Vafa integrality discussion and the comparison with the superpolynomial
contents.reason: The GSV/DGR integrality conjectures concern integer-valued link invariants beyond the comparison of the two homology theories and are not needed by any item of this pair.
